finding.text: A stale comment in the module this diff changes: `List.js` `ref()`'s block comment (worktree qf-1, `core/List/List.js:319-323`) still says `ref()` links "instead of re-parenting it the way `add(x)` still does (D13, 2026-11-02: switching `add()`'s own default is a later, separate merge…)". That stopped being true in this same diff. A fresh agent reading the code would believe `add()` still moves an item. One line fixes it: "`add(x)` now does the same (2026-11-09); `ref()` is the explicit form."

Demo ask 3 ("a small line naming where it really lives: Ref → list A / item id") is met only as raw JSON. List B shows `{"type":"Ref","path":"a.shared"}` under "what List B actually stores:" (shots/…/400.png, List B card). That proves what is stored, but a new coder has to decode `a.shared` themselves. Add a plain line such as "Ref → list a / item shared" above the JSON.

`public/live/demos/ref/files.jsonl` lists `shots/`, but the repo's `.gitignore:213` (`**/shots/`) ignores that folder. So the 400 and 1200 shots the brief asked for are on disk in the worktree but in no commit, and on a clone the listed file entry points at nothing. Either drop the `shots/` line, or accept it as the repo's convention for every demo.

`/live/demos/` (`public/live/demos/page.jsonl`) only has `{"file":"ref/"}` lines. Every other demo there has a `part-link` card (for example `codecard1`), and this one has none. The brief keeps the `/live/` link for the mastermind, so this is a reminder to add the card on `/live/demos/` too. Until then the demo is only reachable from the two doc links.

The guard in `List.add` is `x.parent && this.index_of(x) === -1`. That is broader than the brief's wording ("a parent that is a List other than this"). An item held in a slot (`adopt_slot`), not in any list, now also becomes a Ref when added to a list. The census found no such caller, and a Ref is the safe result, so this is recorded as a note only.
At 1200 and wider, the h3 "List A — owns the item" wraps to 2 lines (layout.json `wraps` at 1200/1920/3440), while the List B heading fits on 1. So the two cards' headings don't line up.
The intro paragraph shouts with capitals ("BOTH", "THROUGH"). Bold or plain words would read calmer (content: tone).
